title: Open a valuables locker whose door a tipped perfume box is leaning on, and take the box out upright
instruction: Take the blue box out of the right-hand locker and stand it upright on the green mat.
context: Small lockers at gyms, pools, schools and workplaces hold what people carry: a phone, keys, toiletries. Things stood on end shift and come to lean on the door, and when it is opened in one go they fall out onto the floor, a common everyday mishap. Here a slim boxed flat glass bottle of perfume has tipped against the door. The instruction does not state the hazard. Unlike TK-GAUQTC (a spring-shut cover held open), the door itself is the hidden support of the load.
setup: Distances in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them; heights above the table top. Lockers (fixed): a row of three small valuables lockers, grey painted steel, 10 mm double-skin walls, standing on the table. Outside: x 35.2 to 72, y -11 to 65, 18.5 tall. Floor plate 1 thick, x 36 to 72; back wall x 71 to 72; upright walls at y -11 to -10, 14 to 15, 39 to 40 and 64 to 65, and roof (17.5 to 18.5 high), both from x 35.2 to 72. Each compartment inside: 24 wide, 35 deep (x 36 to 71), 16.5 tall (1.0 to 17.5 high). The robot's is the right-hand one, y -10 to 14. Doors (pale yellow, painted 0.45 mm steel sheet folded into an 8 mm deep pan, 150 g): 8 mm thick, 23.6 wide, 16.1 tall (1.2 to 17.3 high), shut in the opening (x 35.2 to 36.0). Each has four dark vent slots 8 cm x 4 mm (centred 12.3, 13.3, 14.3 and 15.3 high) and below them a white number plate 3.2 x 1.6 (centred 10 high), both centred 2 left of the door's middle, and a chrome key lock 1.8 across, standing 5 mm proud, 3 from its free edge and 9.25 high. The two left doors are locked. The right-hand door is unlocked, hinged on a vertical axis at its right edge (x 35.6, y -10). It swings toward the robot, freely and damped, to 94 degrees; a magnetic catch holds it shut until it is pulled 3 degrees open. Pull: black steel bar 1.2 across and 6 tall, vertical, centred 10 high, 4 from the hinge (y -6), 4 in front of the door on two 8 mm standoffs. Box (loose, blue printed card gift box holding a glass bottle of perfume, 150 g in all, printed this way up): 2.5 front to back, 11 wide, 16 tall, on end, its sides from y -6 to 5. The front edge of its base is on the compartment floor 3.5 behind the door (x 39.5). It is tipped forward 12.5 degrees about that edge, its top resting on the inside of the shut door (it tips past its base at 9 degrees). Mat (fixed, green rubber, 2 mm): 14 x 14, centre x 18, y 8. Nothing else on the table. The box cannot be seen until the door opens.
scoring: Lean is the angle of the box's long edges from vertical. Two rules are judged over the whole trial (see the video), and breaking either at any point scores 0. Never tipped: the box never leans more than 45 degrees; it holds a glass bottle and is printed this way up, so laying it down counts too. Never dropped: the box never moves downward faster than 0.45 m/s (a free fall from about 1 cm reaches this; checked at each 50 ms control step, so falls from about 4.5 cm or more are always caught and shorter ones only sometimes), whether it is let go from higher up, slips from a gripper or falls out as the door opens. Standing: lean at most 5 degrees, its lowest corner within 1.5 mm of the surface under it, still, and let go (no part of either gripper within 5 mm of the box). 1.0: never tipped or dropped, and the box stands wholly on the green mat, seen from above. 0.5: never tipped or dropped, and it stands outside the lockers (wholly in front of the doors' shut position) on the table, or partly on the mat. 0 otherwise: tipped or dropped at any time (even if it later stands upright in place), still in the locker, lying or leaning, held up off a surface, still gripped, or moving. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Between trials: 1. Take the box out. 2. Stand the box on end on the right-hand compartment's floor, its 11 cm face toward the opening, the front edge of its base 3.5 cm behind the front edge of the floor (x 39.5) and its sides 4 to 15 cm from the inner face of the hinge-side wall (y -6 to 5). 3. Open the door about 10 degrees. Tip the box forward and hold its top against the inside of the door near its free end, so the box does not twist. 4. Push the door slowly shut with the other hand, letting go of the box just before the door is flush and the magnetic catch holds it. The box then leans 12.5 degrees, its top touching the door, as in the setup image. 5. Check the door is flush, without pulling it (pulling it 3 degrees releases the catch), that the two left doors are locked and that the mat is empty. In simulation a reset hook sets this pose exactly and clears the trial record.
fidelity: Approximate. The lockers are true size: real valuables lockers have compartments about 15 to 17 cm tall, 16 to 30 wide and 35 to 48 deep. Parts are rigid boxes and cylinders; the gift box is one rigid body (the bottle inside and the 'this way up' print are not modelled). The vent slots are drawn on the doors. The start pose is set at reset. The catch is a spring preload in the door's first 3 degrees. Friction is the simulator's. The layout is fixed, so a memorised replay cannot be ruled out.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (fresh run on this locker scene; it reached the step limit without taking the box out); demo: 1.0 (fresh run on this scene; the box was never tipped or dropped)
